guitar.notes: Well documented Clapton-era gear; entry accurate.

tone.target: nasal slightly fuzzed British riff tone with thick sustain
tone.profile: nasal slightly fuzzed British riff tone with thick sustain
tone.summary: A classic, aggressive British rock setup using a Marshall-style amp model, boosted by a Red Haze fuzz for bite and thick sustain, paired with a 4x12 cabinet.
corrections: favor riff sustain over generic crunch

rig.name: Cream - Sunshine Of Your Love - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and noise inherent in high-gain British rock tones.
Provide the required 'slight fuzz bite' and nasal aggression while boosting sustain.
Slightly push the signal into the amp model for extra sustain and upper-mid presence.
blocks.gap: Using 'Boost' as a general clean boost to complement the fuzz, mimicking a light treble booster effect.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall/Plexi sound required for vintage British rock.
Provide the necessary 4x12 cabinet voicing for a full, aggressive British rock sound.
Sculpt the tone by emphasizing upper-mids and maintaining clarity while keeping the core riff punch.
Optional subtle thickening for added depth (kept off by default).
blocks.gap: Not essential to the core riff tone, but useful for adding dimension if needed.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space and vintage room ambience without muddying the riff.
blocks.gap: The requirement was to 'keep it dry,' so this reverb is kept minimal and used only for depth, not wash.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the aggressive, nasal bite and sustain required for vintage British rock.

proposals.reason: Enhance the aggressive, nasal bite and upper-mid presence needed for Cream's tone.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and punch in the high end.
